name: Power Night Recap
about: Fast night-event recap: 79 held shots and 163 picture changes in 51.4 seconds, cream flash pops, bokeh-plate wipes, warm low-key grade, striped black-and-white run, small caps subtitles, corner logo, logo stutter ending.

reference.credit: Reference reel by @ebonymagazine. Plays from Instagram. No footage, music, logo or words from it are stored in this style.

score: 720×1280 (9:16), 23.976 fps, 1232 frames, 51.38 s. H.264 High, 8-bit 4:2:0, Rec.709, about 1.7 Mbps video. HE-AAC stereo 44.1 kHz at 71 kbps. This is Instagram's re-encode; the camera and export settings behind it are gone.

79 held shots of 4 frames or more, plus 85 segments of 1 to 3 frames (flash, plate and stutter frames): 163 picture changes in 51.4 s, about 3.2 a second. Median held shot 0.54 s. The selfie run is the only slow section (1.5 events a second); every other section runs 3 to 4.5.

41 hard cuts, 30 cream flash pops, 9 bokeh-plate wipes, 2 two-frame grey dips, one whip frame. The flash is cream, rgb(229,212,180), not white. Opens on a roll-whip and a 10-frame light-streak strobe; closes on a 4-shot logo stutter.

A face is in 82% of shots; 51% are a single person. Faces sit in the upper third (centre at 36% from the top) and near the middle left-to-right. Tight framing dominates: 30 close, 16 medium close, 15 medium, 16 wide or no person.

58% of shots have a deliberate move (push in, pull out, pan or tilt); 17 are handheld drift and 15 are locked off. Push in is the most common single move. Moves are short and continue through the cut.

No camera data in the file, so f-stop, focal length and shutter cannot be read. Backgrounds fall out of focus behind nearly every person at night, the look of a fast lens wide open (roughly f/1.4 to f/2.8 full-frame). Three glass-ball shots are confirmed by eye (frames 65-68, 640-646, 1084-1093). City inserts are long-exposure light trails. A trained guess, not a reading.
Low-key. Middle brightness sits at 9% and average at 18%. About 19% of each frame is crushed to near-black. Whites top out near 71%, with almost nothing clipped. Dark frame, bright skin and wardrobe.

Warm. Shadows average rgb(10,6,8), mids rgb(48,30,28), highlights rgb(136,113,94): red-brown mids, cream highlights, near-neutral blacks. Saturation averages 53%. Orange-red is the lead colour in 74% of colour shots; blue and cyan stage light is the accent. The average hides two palettes: arrivals and portraits are warm cream and brown against teal walls; inside the room is deep blue, purple and red stage light.

Fine vertical stripes with a 4.7-pixel pitch (about 153 lines across the frame) sit over the selfie run and the black-and-white run. Black-and-white is warm, not neutral: highlights read cream. No added vignette was found. Grain is too light to separate from Instagram's compression.

Corner logo on every frame, 84x47 px, centre 82.6% across and 13.2% down. Subtitles are white small caps, letters 16 px tall, centred, 73.5% down, one line, no box, 18 lines that follow the spoken words. The title card lasts 8 frames at 27.0 s. Logo on black for the last 62 frames (2.6 s).

-14.2 LUFS, 7.5 LU range, true peak +1.2 dB (slight clipping). Voice covers 28 of 51 seconds in five blocks, with music-only gaps at 5.9-7.4 s, 13-16 s, 24.6-28.1 s and from 37.3 s to the end. Tempo will not lock: two methods read 98 and 120 BPM. Cuts are not on the beat. Flash pops land on a high-frequency hit 33% of the time against 20% by chance, on 30 flashes, which hints at a whoosh or shutter sound but does not prove it. Last 0.8 s is silent.

Roll-whip open and strobe (0-1.5 s). Arrivals and place (1.5-7.8). Selfie run (7.8-13.2). City inserts (13.2-14.9). Room and first long soundbite, ending on the black-and-white reveal (14.9-24.3). Bar, glass-ball, 8-frame title (24.3-27.6). Dusk, stage and awards under two soundbites (27.6-39.2). Black-and-white stripe run, music only (39.2-42.4). Closing details and the building (42.4-48.3). Logo stutter and end card (48.3-51.4).

moves.name: roll_whip_open
moves.what: Frames 0-21. One high shot of the arrivals carpet with the camera rolling, speeding up into a whip and a brightness spike on the last two frames.
moves.how: Rotate the clip about 0 to 25 degrees over 22 frames with ease-in, add directional blur on the last 3 frames.

moves.name: streak_strobe
moves.what: Frames 22-31. Light-streak plates and black, swapping every 1 to 2 frames for 10 frames.
moves.how: Stack a defocused light-streak clip and a black solid, cut every 2 frames.

moves.name: cream_flash
moves.what: A full-frame cream flash, rgb(229,212,180), 1 to 3 frames, fading into the next shot. Nine frames reach over 72% brightness (32-33, 125, 187, 941, 969-970, 1016, 1073).
moves.rate: 30 flash pops in 51 s; 38% of shot changes
moves.how: Solid colour layer above the picture, opacity 90% then 45% then 0 across 3 frames, on the first frames of the incoming shot.

moves.name: bokeh_plate_wipe
moves.what: One to three frames of an out-of-focus light or bokeh plate between two shots (69-70, 377-378, 416, 429-430, 679-680, 704, 866-868, 931-932).
moves.how: Keep a bin of 10 defocused light plates shot on the night; drop 2 frames between shots.

moves.name: sepia_still_stutter
moves.what: Frames 121-126. Four different sepia city stills, one frame each, then a flash.
moves.how: Four photos, 1 frame each, warm monochrome, flash on the fifth frame.

moves.name: four_frame_insert
moves.what: Held shots of exactly 4 frames used as punctuation (65-68, 127-130, 141-144, 578-581).
moves.how: Trim to 4 frames. Use only on a clear face or object.

moves.name: live_selfie_run
moves.what: Frames 187-315. Four phone live-stream selfies with the app's comment overlay, 13 to 54 frames each, fine vertical stripes over the picture. Pace drops from about 4 events a second to 1.5.
moves.how: Screen-record guests on a live stream, or shoot vertical selfies and overlay a 4.7 px stripe pattern at about 13%.

moves.name: time_jump_colour_flip
moves.what: Frames 322-335. The same street-sign shot cut against itself after the traffic light changes from red to green.
moves.how: Hold a static shot through a light change and cut out the middle.

moves.name: mono_reveal
moves.what: Frames 561-586. The person speaking is shown in warm black-and-white for the end of their line, then one whip frame, then colour fades back over 4 frames.
moves.how: Black-and-white with a cream tint on the last second of a soundbite; keyframe saturation 0 to 100 over 4 frames on the next shot.

moves.name: title_blip
moves.what: Frames 647-654. The title card is on screen for 8 frames (a third of a second), in a gap between voices, 52% of the way through.
moves.how: Title on a dark warm background, 8 frames, flash in.

moves.name: mono_stripe_run
moves.what: Frames 941-1016. Six portraits of 7 to 16 frames, each split from the next by a 1 to 2 frame cream flash, in warm black-and-white with stripes. No voice under it.
moves.how: Six tight portraits, saturation 0, cream tint, stripe overlay, cream flash between every one.

moves.name: logo_match_stutter
moves.what: Frames 1159-1169. Four different shots of the event logo out in the room, 3, 3, 3 and 2 frames, with the logo in the same place each time, landing on the clean logo end card.
moves.how: Shoot the logo on 4 surfaces, scale each so the logo lines up, 3 frames each, cut to logo on black.

moves.name: small_caps_subtitles
moves.what: White small caps subtitles that follow the spoken words phrase by phrase, 18 lines, letters 16 px tall, centred at 73.5% down. They are timed to speech, not to picture cuts.
moves.rate: 18 lines over the 28 s of voice
moves.how: Subtitle track, tracking about +100, no background box.

moves.name: corner_bug
moves.what: Small logo top right on every frame, including black frames, 84x47 px.
moves.how: Logo on the top video track for the whole sequence.

absent: No beat sync. Held-shot starts land on a beat 31% of the time against 34% by chance, on a bass hit 22% against 23%, on an onset 31% against 32% (5,000 random times).
No drop and no breath before one. Level stays within a few dB from 7 s to 48 s.
Cutting does not slow down under the voice: 3.2 events a second with voice, 3.3 without.
No typography strobe. The only title is the 8-frame card.
No letterbox bars and no repeated frames in the live action, so nothing points to a frame-rate mismatch.

shoot: Vertical, 4K if you can, 23.976 or 24 fps, shutter 1/50. Fast prime wide open for people (f/1.4 to f/2.8); this is a guess at what they used, and it is what gives the soft backgrounds.

About 80 usable shots for 51 seconds: 30 tight portraits, 12 moments (hugs, handshakes, applause), 8 details (drinks, watch, trophy, decks), 6 wides, 6 stage shots, 6 phone selfies, 4 city shots, 3 of the building or sign, and the logo on 4 different surfaces.
Ten out-of-focus light plates (rack focus off stage lights or traffic) for the wipes and the strobe.
Three or four short interviews, 6 to 9 seconds each, plus one host welcome line. Record clean audio.
Push in on people. Over half the shots have a move; push in is the most used.
Expose dark: keep the room black and let skin and wardrobe carry the light.
cut: Sequence 1080x1920, 23.976 fps. Lay the voice first: welcome line, selfie chatter, then three soundbites with 2 to 3 second music gaps between them.
Cut picture at about 3 changes a second right through, voice or no voice. Median shot 13 frames. Do not chase the beat; this reel does not.
Put a cream flash on roughly every third cut, a bokeh plate on every eighth.
Reveal a speaker in black-and-white at the end of their line. Save the striped black-and-white run for the music-only stretch near the end.
Title card for 8 frames in a voice gap at the halfway mark. End on the 4-shot logo stutter into logo on black for 2.6 seconds.
Subtitles in small caps under every spoken phrase. Corner logo on the top track for the whole piece.
Grade on one adjustment layer: crush about a fifth of the frame to black, cap whites near 70%, warm the mids. Master to -14 LUFS with true peak under -1 dB (the reference clips at +1.2).

story.frame: You are being let into the room. The brand is the host, the guests are the proof, and the award show itself is almost background. The caption on the post says the same thing: this is a room to aspire to be in. The event's 2026 theme was 'The Stories We Shape', and the edit is built so the guests tell the story in their own voices while the brand's logo never leaves the corner.
story.context: The 2026 EBONY Power 100 gala, 9 November 2026, Hollywood Palladium, Los Angeles (press coverage). Made by the production house A² Creators (@austins.atelier), which lists four video editors for the production: German Vizcarra, Patrick Merluzzi, Vadim Dzhavadov and Imani Austin, with Imani Austin as production lead and lead camera and Alexander John as executive producer. The captions do not say which editor cut this reel. Signs read off the frames: the venue's neon sign, the 'Sunset' street sign, a sponsor wall, the event wordmark.
beats: A host's voice welcomes you over one spinning high shot of the carpet, then a strobe and a flash drop you beside the first arrival.
Gowns, the car, the neon sign, the marquee. It says where you are and that it is expensive before anyone speaks again.
Four phone live-stream captures from the carpet, raw and loud, with the brand's own account visible in the comments. The edit slows down here on purpose so the excitement reads as real, not produced.
Skyline, street sign, palms, a car pulling up. Night falls; you move from outside to inside.

The first full soundbite, about the brand showing a community's achievements to the world, plays over the room and the audience. The speaker's face is held back until the end of her line, in black-and-white.
Drinks, the glass-ball shot, and the title for a third of a second. It works as a chapter break.
A second voice talks about seeing so many icons in one place, and the picture answers with the stage, the performers and a trophy changing hands. A third voice calls it a favourite night of the year.
Voices stop. Six black-and-white portraits, a flash between each. This is the yearbook page, the part people screenshot and tag.
An honoree at the podium, a watch, an embrace, the room emptying into the after-party, the building from outside.
The logo four ways, then alone on black.
story.how_to_find_the_frame: Read the voice first, not the pictures. List who speaks and what each line claims. Then check what the picture shows under each line. Here every line is a guest praising the room, and the stage is never shown with its own sound, so the subject is belonging, not the ceremony.

tutorial.level: This is a mid-level edit made to look high-end by discipline. Nothing in it needs a paid plug-in. The hard parts are the shooting (soft backgrounds at night, light plates, the glass ball) and the voice selection.
effects: Cream flash
A solid colour clip, rgb(229,212,180), on the track above the picture. Opacity 90%, 45%, 0% over three frames.
Premiere: Color Matte. Resolve: Solid Color generator. CapCut: a cream image on an overlay track. Kit file: cream.png.
Light plates
Real footage: rack the lens out of focus on stage lights or traffic for a few seconds. You need about ten.
No effect. Shoot them. Cut 1 to 3 frames between shots.
Streak strobe
A light plate and black, swapped every 1 to 2 frames for 10 frames.
Razor the plate into 2-frame pieces and delete every other piece over a black background.
Roll whip
Rotation from 0 to about 25 degrees over 22 frames, slow then fast, with motion blur on the last three.
Premiere: Transform effect with its own shutter angle at 180 to 360. Resolve: Transform keyframes plus a directional blur. CapCut: rotation keyframes plus a blur.
Warm black-and-white
Saturation to zero, then tint the highlights cream.
Any colour tool. For agents: hue=s=0, then colorchannelmixer rr=1.0 gg=0.93 bb=0.80.
Stripes
Thin vertical black lines every 4.7 pixels at 720 wide (7 pixels at 1080), about 13% strength.
Kit file: stripes-1080x1920.png on the track above the clip. Only on the selfie run and the black-and-white run.
Colour bloom
Saturation keyframed from 0 to 100 over four frames at the start of a shot.
Keyframe saturation on the clip.
Glass ball
A real crystal ball held in front of the lens. Three shots.
Shoot it. A fisheye or lens-distortion effect is a weak stand-in.
Grey dip
A two-frame cross dissolve.
Default dissolve, length 2 frames.
Subtitles
White capitals, small (letters 1.2% of frame height), wide letter spacing, centred, 73.5% down, no box, one line.
Caption track or text clips. Tracking about +100. One phrase at a time, on with the words and off with them.
Corner logo
Logo at 82.6% across and 13.2% down, 11.7% of frame width, on every frame.
Top track for the whole timeline.
Grade
On one adjustment layer over everything: pull the blacks down until about a fifth of the frame is black, cap the whites near 70%, warm the mid-tones.
Premiere: Adjustment Layer with Lumetri. Resolve: Adjustment Clip or a timeline node.
Logo stutter
The logo filmed on four different surfaces, each scaled so it sits in the same place, 3 frames each (the last one 2), then the logo on black for 2.6 seconds.
Position and scale by eye against a guide. No effect needed.
steps: 1. Set up
Timeline 1080x1920, 23.976 fps. Tracks from the top: logo, subtitles, flashes and stripes, adjustment layer for the grade, picture, light plates, voice, music.
2. Lay the voice first

Welcome line at the head (about 6 s). Selfie audio from 7.8 s (about 5.5 s). Three soundbites starting near 16 s, 28 s and 35 s. Leave music-only gaps of 1.5 to 3.5 s between blocks and stop all voice by 37 s. Total voice about 28 s.
3. Music under
One track, no drop needed. Keep it under the voice and let it come up in the gaps. Do not cut to its beat.
4. Cold open
One wide with the roll whip (22 frames), the streak strobe (10 frames), a three-frame cream flash, land on your best full-length arrival.
5. Build the sections

Use the section table: arrivals and place, selfie run, city breath, room under soundbite one, drinks and title, stage and awards under soundbites two and three, portrait wall, afterglow, logo. Fill each with shots of 10 to 13 frames. Use the shot sheet for the exact lengths.
6. Slow the selfie run
Four takes of 13 to 54 frames. Keep the phone audio. Add the stripes. No flashes inside this section.
7. Punctuate

Cream flash on about every third cut, always on the incoming shot. A light plate on about every eighth cut. Four 4-frame inserts on clear faces or objects. Two grey dips inside the dark interior section.
8. Hold the speaker back
Run each soundbite over other pictures and show the speaker only at the end of the line. Make the first reveal black-and-white, then bloom the colour back on the next shot.
9. Title
Eight frames, in the voice gap near the halfway mark, flash in.
10. Portrait wall
In the first music-only stretch after the last soundbite: six tight portraits of 7 to 16 frames, black-and-white with stripes, a full cream flash between each.
11. Close
Two or three slower shots (one can run 30 frames), the building, the logo stutter, logo on black for 62 frames with the sound fading to silence.
12. Subtitles and logo
Subtitle every spoken phrase. Logo on the top track from first frame to the frame before the end card.
13. Grade and master
Grade on the adjustment layer only. Master to -14 LUFS with true peak under -1 dB. The reference peaks at +1.2 dB, which is a fault.
14. Check it
Count picture changes per second (target 3 to 4.5 outside the selfie run), flashes (about 30), and that no subtitle is on screen without speech.
agent: Load web/styles/power-night-recap.json. shots[] is the timeline: t0 and dur in seconds at fps 23.976; type says what kind of clip to place; look is one of color, stripe, mono, mono-stripe, orb, strobe, logo-stutter; tin is the transition on the incoming shot (kind flash|smear|black, frames, peak 0-1).
Place voice before picture using voice[] (start, end in seconds). Never place a caption outside a voice block; captions[] gives the windows.
Flash: overlay a solid of flash_rgb for tin.frames + 1 frames with alpha = peak * (1 - n / (frames + 1)).
Mono: hue=s=0 then colorchannelmixer=rr=1.0:gg=0.93:bb=0.80. Stripe: overlay kit/power-night-recap/stripes-<size>.png.
Grade last, on the whole frame, never per clip. Loudness: loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1:LRA=7.
Verify the render with tools/frames.py and tools/audio3.py and compare with sections[] before calling it done.
Do not use any footage, audio, logo or wording from the reference reel.

demo.credit: Billo cut · Billy Sorrells' own footage, cut by the style file. No reference footage.
demo.note: This cut does the hard cuts, cream flashes, stripes, warm black-and-white, blur plates, whip blur, title, corner logo and logo ending. The camera roll in the open, sepia stutter, grey dip and colour flip are not built yet, so they have no clip.
